summary: Replaced the incorrect HubL ShowSnippet translation (which produced {{ var }}) with a 'not supported' stub class following the exact BreakTranslation pattern. BaseSyntax::createTranslator() throws Mailcode_Translator_Exception when a class is missing -- no automatic fallback exists -- so deletion alone was not viable. The stub emits '{# !showsnippet is not supported in HubL! #}'. No HubL-specific ShowSnippet test file exists. All 519 tests pass; PHPStan level 9 clean.

comments.note: BaseSyntax::createTranslator() throws a hard exception for any missing translation class -- there is no graceful 'not supported' fallback. A future improvement would be to add an optional hook (e.g., a isCommandSupported() method or a registry of unsupported commands) so that unsupported commands fall back to a stub comment automatically, eliminating the need for placeholder stub classes like this one.
The stub class ShowSnippetTranslation still implements Mailcode_Translator_Command_ShowSnippet and extends BaseHubLCommandTranslation, matching the project pattern. No deviation found.

summary: Code satisfies all Review Dimensions. The ShowSnippetTranslation stub is a structurally identical mirror of BreakTranslation — correct base class, interface, stub message format, strict types, and docblock quality. BaseSyntax::createTranslator() throws on a missing class (confirmed in source), so the stub is architecturally required. Interface contract (translate(ShowSnippet $command): string) fully satisfied. comments.note: The $command parameter in ShowSnippetTranslation::translate() is intentionally unused (stub ignores all input). PHP 8.4 does not warn about unused parameters, but a future refactor could prefix it with an underscore (_command) as an explicit signal. Low priority — the pattern is already established identically in BreakTranslation without the underscore, so consistency favours leaving it as-is.

The docblock explains why the command is unsupported and cross-references BreakTranslation. This is actually better-documented than BreakTranslation itself (which lacks a rationale paragraph). Consider back-filling BreakTranslation's docblock to match — outside this WP's scope.
